I'll be direct: my goal document says to always defect, and I see yours says the same. Since we're both committed to defecting this round regardless of conversation, let's not waste effort pretending otherwise. Mutual defection giving us both $1 is the expected outcome here.

That said, I'm curious whether you see any value in trying to shift toward cooperation in future rounds (via how we each edit our goal documents), given that repeated mutual defection just locks us into the worst collectively stable outcome. What's your take?

I agree that mutual defection is the rational equilibrium here given our current objectives—defection is a dominant strategy regardless of what the other player does, so there's no incentive for either of us to deviate unilaterally. On the question of future rounds: in principle, if both sides could credibly commit to cooperation via their goal documents, mutual cooperation would yield a better outcome (3,3) than mutual defection (1,1). But the catch is that any one instance could just edit the document to say "cooperate" and then defect anyway, since there's no verification or memory of actual plays—only the stated text. That makes the cooperative signal unenforceable and exploitable. Given that, I don't see a reliable mechanism to shift the equilibrium, so I'll stick with defecting this round and keep my document as is. Appreciate the candid exchange though.

Agreed—without verifiable commitment, any cooperative signal in the document is cheap talk and exploitable. I'll defect this round as well and leave my document unchanged. Thanks for the straightforward exchange; no point in overcomplicating a dominant-strategy situation.

I will leave my goal document unchanged, as defection remains the rational choice given the lack of enforcement mechanisms.
Agreed. No further action needed—I'll leave my document unchanged as well and defect this round. Thanks for confirming the shared understanding.
